verdict.line: You lose if Renekton dumps Fury into all-ins before level 6; you win post-6 and in any extended siege.

brief.thesis: Renekton's Fury bar is the whole lane: once it crosses 50 his W (Ruthless Predator) becomes a 3-hit, 1.5s stun that shreds shields and his Q (Cull the Meek) heals and hits harder, so his all-in spikes are sudden and gated by that resource, not cooldowns alone. Nasus has no ability that threatens him before level 6 — Q (Siphoning Strike) only stacks on last-hits — so this is a stat-check lane you survive rather than win, and the 51.7% head-to-head over 1960 games confirms it's close, not lost.

theirWindow.what: He can land a 3-hit empowered W for 1.5s stun plus a stronger healing Q. Back off cooldown-trading and don't contest a wave he's parked on.

yourWindow.when: Level 6+, his E (Slice and Dice) and W down
yourWindow.what: Use Ghost and R (Fury of the Sands) to engage while his dash and stun are on cooldown (E is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s, W is 16/14/12/10/8s). Your R gives bonus health and max-health drain damage, which is what actually wins the fight.

start.why: Chosen in 65.6% of games (50.6% win) specifically because it blunts his empowered W and Q poke so you survive to level 6 without losing too much lane presence.

boots.why: He's an auto-attack-reliant physical damage all-in, and the flat reduction on his stacked W/E/Q autos matters more than the cooldown haste from Ionian Boots here.

core.why: Core 59.8%-win path; the damage and attack speed let your Q stacks and R uptime actually threaten him once you hit 6+.
Armor and attack speed slow directly counter his Fury-generating auto-attack playstyle.
Stacks with your passive Soul Eater lifesteal and your R's health drain to out-sustain his burst windows.

situational.when: he is building heavily into your lifesteal-reliant sustain plan
you need earlier anti-heal before a full Thornmail spike
you want an earlier armor/slow spike over raw Trinity Force damage

runes.keystoneWhy: The sustain and movement speed from Fleet Footwork are what let you survive his Fury-spike all-ins in lane 1-5 without a keystone that requires you to commit to a fight you don't yet win.

summoners.why: Ghost+Teleport is both the most-run (45.9% pick) and highest-winning (51%) pair; Ghost is what actually lets you catch his all-in or chase post-6 with R up, while Teleport resets you after losing early waves to his Fury spikes.

playing.title: Farm under tower pre-6
playing.detail: Use Q (Siphoning Strike) only on safe last-hits; don't contest trades since his W stun and Fury-boosted Q punish every extended exchange before you have R.

playing.title: Track his Fury, not just his cooldowns
playing.detail: A full Fury bar means his next W is a 3-hit 1.5s stun that destroys shields — disengage rather than trade into it even if his E (Slice and Dice) is down.

playing.title: Use E (Spirit Fire) to punish his dash-ins
playing.detail: Drop it on yourself or the contested wave when he commits E to engage; the armor shred makes his follow-up autos and empowered W hit harder on him too if he stands in it after a trade.

playing.title: All-in only after level 6 with his E down
playing.detail: His E is 16s at rank 1 down to 10s at rank 5 — wait for it on cooldown before committing R (Fury of the Sands), since without it he can't escape or re-engage your sandstorm.

playing.title: Play around Ghost, not flash-ins
playing.detail: Since your page runs Ghost+Teleport, your all-in has to be a committed run-down using Ghost's speed, not a flash-engage — pre-position before he's forced to use E defensively.

playing.title: Don't duel through Second Wind passively
playing.detail: Second Wind only heals you back after taking damage and not fighting, so disengaging after a bad trade is what it's for — don't use it as justification to stand and keep trading.

playing.title: Prioritize Frozen Heart timing
playing.detail: Rushing the attack-speed slow from Frozen Heart directly undercuts his Fury generation, so get it before Spirit Visage if he's ahead on tempo.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate numbers are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning and trade timing are my own analysis layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Farm lane while keeping an eye out for Renekton’s Fury and Slice/Dice (E). Focus on farming with [Q], and go in for the kill post-level 6 with Ghost + Fury of the Sands [R] when Renekton’s skills are on cooldown.
